QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_50

question.text: Mr. Manish Kale, Manager of Sahyadri Ventures (Cat I VC), is drafting the first annual LP report and is concerned about the level of detail on under-performing investee companies. Which of the following BEST captures the dilemma that Chapter 12 identifies for fund managers in fund reporting?

answer.text: There is no dilemma — managers should publish all investee internals in full to LPs and the media.

There is a tension between the statutory obligation to disclose (to maintain investor relationships and good standards) and the business need to maintain confidentiality to protect portfolio-company data privacy, competitive edge, and pipeline, with risk of legal complications from information leakage.
The only dilemma is which font to use in the report.
Managers should decline all disclosure if performance is weak, since weak performance is not a disclosable item.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 12 (Section 12.3.1 'Conflicts and Concerns in Fund Reporting'): 'Managers may be reluctant to disclose all information ... on the one hand, there is a statutory obligation to disclose ... on the other hand, further information, especially at a level of detail that allows an independent risk assessment, may potentially impact follow-on fund raising if the fund performance is not progressing well. There is also a rationale for maintaining confidentiality to ensure portfolio companies are protected by data privacy ... too much information given out could dilute the competitive edge of their portfolio companies ... legal complications arising from leakage of proprietary fund information.' The Trap: Option A (full media disclosure) violates confidentiality and insider-trading norms. Options C and D are caricatures — weak performance IS disclosable per Regulation 22(a)/(d). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the same dilemma. XV (Research Analyst) treats the selective-disclosure angle from analyst perspective. XXIV (AML) handles a different confidentiality-vs-disclosure tension (SAR filing). Manager's Pro-Tip: Use TIERED disclosure: aggregate sector / stage reporting in broadly-shared decks, company-level details in password-protected LP portals (with NDAs), and full IC memos only to LPAC members. This lets you comply with Regulation 22 while protecting deal competitiveness.
